stories.summary: DeepSeek announced V4.1-Flash-1017 on X on October 17, calling it a minor update to V4.1-Flash with stronger reasoning, coding and agentic scores. The 763B-parameter checkpoint's weights are on Hugging Face and ModelScope under the MIT licence, and its own benchmark table claims 77.0 on DeepSWE v1.1, ahead of Claude Opus 5's 74.0 on that test. DeepSeek also opened its own Search and Fetch APIs to all developers at $0.75 per 1,000 calls.
stories.title: DeepSeek ships V4.1-Flash-1017 with MIT open weights and search APIs

stories.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Slides on October 16, letting eligible Pro, Business and Enterprise users with Space access create and co-edit presentations in real time. Users can leave shared comments, present directly from ChatGPT, and export to PowerPoint, PDF, Google Slides or Keynote. The launch extends ChatGPT's workspace tools alongside Docs and other collaboration surfaces introduced in Space.
stories.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Slides with real-time co-editing

stories.summary: A Michigan-based recruiter named Jason went viral after sharing a clip on X on October 16 showing him confronting a suspected deepfake job candidate during a remote interview. When his coworker noticed glitched glasses and a ghosted second frame, Jason asked the candidate to wave a hand in front of his face — the classic John Cena 'You Can't See Me' test — and the candidate allegedly avoided doing so. The incident has sparked fresh debate over AI misuse in remote hiring.
stories.title: Recruiter catches deepfake job candidate with hand-wave test

stories.summary: Videos claiming to show Iranian fishermen retrieving iPhones and perfumes from a sunken cargo ship went viral online, gathering millions of views. An Al Jazeera investigation found the clips were AI-generated. The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride did sink on October 14 after a fire, but all 21 crew members were rescued safely — none of the viral footage was real.
stories.title: AI-generated iPhone shipwreck videos go viral; Al Jazeera debunks them

stories.summary: vLLM and NVIDIA are reporting 842 tokens per second for the Kimi K3 model running on 16 GB300 GPUs, a headline number that has been making the rounds. The figure assumes a synthetic speculative-decoding acceptance length of 6, so it is aggregate decode throughput and excludes prefill — not a measurement on real prompts. Without speculation, the reported gains over the baseline are 1.5 to 2x.
stories.title: Kimi K3 hits 842 tokens/s on vLLM — but only with synthetic decoding

stories.summary: NVIDIA's RTX Spark laptops have started shipping from $2,599, packing 1 petaflop of FP4 compute and 128GB of unified memory. The machines are positioned squarely at local AI workloads, taking aim at Apple's lead in on-device frontier inference. The launch pairs with Apple demoing the full 816B Muse Spark Open running locally on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios at 36+ tokens per second.
stories.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops ship from $2,599 with 128GB unified memory
